title: Review of c30's Hash Chemistry O calibration: replicated on fresh seeds 31-32 (raw novelty hash 64-79k vs biased random 347k; cohort new activity 46-58 vs shadow 13-18 early, then ~0 to t=6000); the world is not deterministic for a given seed
summary: Looked at o_calibration_2000.png and o_long_20000.png first. Re-ran the claim's simulate.py on fresh seeds and analysed the logs with its own o_measure.stats and RB shadow (analyse.py, review_stats.json): hash (mode 0) seeds 31 and 32 to t=2000 and seed 31 to t=6000, biased random U[0.2,1] seed 31, fair random U[0,1] seed 31; labkit packs on seeds 31 (extinct by t=80) and 32 (rerun32/). Fair random extinct at t=5. Raw distinct k>=2 multisets at t=2000: hash 63972-78886, biased random 347167 (claim 78-90k vs 344-348k): hash is lowest, as claimed. Cohort new activity (a*=50, L=1000, 200-step windows): hash 46 and 56 in the first window against shadow 13 and 18, then mostly 0 (one burst of 45 at t=800-1000 in seed 31); random 15 vs shadow 12. Long run (seed 31, 1000-step windows): cohort 123 in t<1000 (shadow 24), then 0,0,0,0,0 to t=6000 (shadow 0-1); cumulative Bedau new activity keeps rising (443 vs shadow 28), so the claim's point that late Bedau crossings are old components and the cohort measure shows stasis replicates. Top-20 overlap with t<1000 stays 0.85 (long seed 31) and 0.7-1.0 (seed 32), and falls to 0.05 in one short run.

observations.F: review_stats.json: unique hash 64-79k vs random 347k; cohort hash 46-58 vs shadow 13-18 in t<200, 0 in every 1000-step window from t=1000 to 6000 (shadow 0-1); fair random extinct at t=5; rerun32/sheet.png soup of particles to t=2000

seeds_run.result: pass at T=6000 (stasis after t<1000); early extinction at T=2000 in another process (matches the claimed early-extinction rate)

controls_run.F: RB neutral shadow per run (claim's o_measure.shadow), biased and fair random-fitness worlds on seed 31

verdicts.limitation: The world is not deterministic for a given seed: seed 31 at T=2000 run twice in one process ends at pop 3404 and 3301, and went extinct at t=13 in a separate process while the T=6000 run with the same seed survives (nondeterminism.txt). Per-seed counts such as '1/9 extinct' and per-seed numbers therefore cannot be reproduced exactly; the statistics I checked hold across runs. Some numba or Python-side RNG is probably unseeded (world.py _seed seeds only one RNG). labkit sheets show bright lines along the left and top domain edges in most frames (rerun32/sheet.png), possibly particles clamped to the boundary or a rendering artifact; I did not trace it. I ran 3 hash runs, not 9, and did not rerun the evoloop census.
